summary:
Fleetwood Mac’s 1975 self-titled album introduced Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks to the band and launched its most successful lineup. After Bob Welch left in late 1974, Mick Fleetwood invited Buckingham to join; Buckingham agreed only if Nicks could join too. The band recorded the album at Sound City Studios in early 1975 with producer Keith Olsen.

Several tracks, including “Rhiannon,” “I’m So Afraid” and “Monday Morning,” came from Buckingham and Nicks’s earlier work. Christine McVie wrote songs including “Over My Head” and “Warm Ways.” Recording brought creative disagreements, particularly between Buckingham and John McVie over studio decisions.

Released in July 1975 in the United States and August in the United Kingdom, the album produced three US top-20 singles: “Over My Head,” “Rhiannon” and “Say You Love Me.” It reached number one on the Billboard 200 in September 1976 and was certified nine-times platinum in the US. It peaked at number 23 in the UK and was ranked among Rolling Stone’s greatest albums.
